content.title: MLB Opening Day: Full schedule, dates, times and pitching matchups for 2026
content.text: Grab your peanuts and Cracker Jack — first pitch is quickly approaching. After the thrilling World Baseball Classic and weeks of spring training, the MLB season has arrived. While it might not feel like spring in some cities just yet, baseball is a sure sign of the warmer days ahead. So, when exactly is Opening Day? Who is playing on the first day of the new season? And how can you watch all the games? Here's a preview for 2026 MLB Opening Day: When is MLB Opening Day in 2026? MLB Opening Day is officially scheduled for Thursday, March 26, 2026, but some teams will play earlier or later. The season begins on Wednesday, March 25, when the San Francisco Giants host the New York Yankees. There are 11 games scheduled for Thursday, with six teams not playing until Friday. What teams are playing on Opening Day in 2026? Twenty-two of the 30 teams will be playing on Thursday for Opening Day. The aforementioned Yankees and Giants kick things off Wednesday, then there's a trio of series that don't begin until Friday (Athletics at Toronto Blue Jays, Colorado Rockies at Miami Marlins and Kansas City Royals at Atlanta Braves). Every other team will be in action Thursday. 2026 MLB Opening Day schedule, games and probable starters Here are the 15 matchups and probable starting pitchers for Opening Day for each team: Away teamHome teamPitching matchupFirst pitch timeNew York YankeesSan Francisco GiantsMax Fried vs. Logan Webb8:05 p.m. ET (Wednesday)Pittsburgh PiratesNew York MetsPaul Skenes vs. Freddy Peralta1:15 p.m. ET (Thursday)Chicago White SoxMilwaukee BrewersShane Smith vs. Jacob Misiorowski2:10 p.m. ET (Thursday)Washington NationalsChicago CubsCade Cavalli vs. Matthew Boyd2:20 p.m. ET (Thursday)Minnesota TwinsBaltimore OriolesJoe Ryan vs. Trevor Rogers3:05 p.m. ET (Thursday)Boston Red SoxCincinnati RedsGarrett Crochet vs. Andrew Abbott4:10 p.m. ET (Thursday)Los Angeles AngelsHouston AstrosJose Soriano vs. Hunter Brown4:10 p.m. ET (Thursday)Detroit TigersSan Diego PadresTarik Skubal vs. Nick Pivetta4:10 p.m. ET (Thursday)Texas RangersPhiladelphia PhilliesNathan Eovaldi vs. Cristopher Sanchez4:15 p.m. ET (Thursday)Tampa Bay RaysSt. Louis CardinalsDrew Rasmussen vs. Matthew Liberatore4:15 p.m. ET (Thursday)Arizona DiamondbacksLos Angeles DodgersZac Gallen vs. Yoshinobu Yamamoto8:30 p.m. ET (Thursday)Cleveland GuardiansSeattle MarinersTanner Bibee vs. Logan Gilbert10:10 p.m. ET (Thursday)AthleticsToronto Blue JaysLuis Severino vs. Kevin Gausman7:07 p.m. ET (Friday)Colorado RockiesMiami MarlinsKyle Freeland vs. Sandy Alcantara7:10 p.m. ET (Friday)Kansas City RoyalsAtlanta BravesCole Ragans vs. Chris Sale7:15 p.m. ET (Friday) How to watch MLB Opening Day 2026 Three games will air nationally on Opening Day: Yankees-Giants on Wednesday, plus Pirates-Mets and Diamondbacks-Dodgers on Thursday. Yankees-Giants will be the first MLB game to air on Netflix to kick off the season. The broadcast crew will include Matt Vasgersian (play-by-play), CC Sabathia (booth analyst), Hunter Pence (booth analyst), Barry Bonds (studio analyst), Albert Pujols (studio analyst) and Anthony Rizzo (studio analyst). The Thursday games will both air on NBC and Peacock as part of the network's return to baseball. Vasgersian (play-by-play) will call Pirates-Mets alongside analysts Al Leiter and Neil Walker.
